mainEntity.name: When do I need a full barn instead of a simple run-in shed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Run-in sheds suit pastured horses needing basic shelter, whereas full barns are best for managed feeding, grooming, and intense weather protection. A run-in shed is cost-effective and provides open turnout, allowing horses to escape direct sun or wind on their own schedule. A full enclosed barn becomes necessary if you need individual stalls for injured horses, secure feed and tack storage, veterinary treatment areas, or freeze-resistant plumbing for automatic waterers. Many owners start with run-ins and add enclosed barns as their herd or riding needs grow.
acceptedAnswer.description: Choose a run-in shed for low-maintenance pasture shelter, but build a full barn if you need individual stall care, secure tack storage, wash racks, and utilities.
